chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sinani (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Kufi quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Al-Hassan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Arafa, who said:

I asked Al-Ridha (peace be upon him): 'Did God create things using His Might or without it?' The Imam (peace be upon him) replied: 'It is not permissible to say that He created things using Might, because when you say that God created things using Might, you are considering His Might to be something other than Him, and you have made it a tool with which He creates things, and this is polytheism. And when you say that He created things without Might, you are describing Him as having made them by means of power over them and might, but He is not weak, nor incapable, nor in need of others. Rather, He is Glorified, and Mighty in His essence, not via an external power.'
ai.seo_question: Is God's power an external tool or part of His essence according to Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (peace be upon him) elucidates the doctrine of divine simplicity by rejecting the Ash'ari concept of 'attributes as distinct entities,' arguing that treating Power as a separate tool for creation introduces multiplicity into the Divine Essence, akin to polytheism. He affirms that God is Mighty by His very essence (li-dhatihi), not by an external power, thereby preserving absolute unity (Tawhid) while avoiding the implication of weakness or need. This hadith serves as a cornerstone for Shia theological debates on whether divine attributes are identical to the Essence or distinct from it.
